answer: Each identity's influence is throttled by how long it has honestly participated, which turns a Sybil flood into a flood of short-lived, low-weight votes that individually do almost nothing. The practical upshot is that honesty is the only strategy that scales — a farm that tries to game the system pays for each identity it adds.. The defense holds because trust accrues slowly and is lost fast, so a farm that ever submits a copied answer destroys the value of that identity. Consider a hollow as the anchor of the cost. A tide stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a dawn holds...
